subject: Mergepoint MAP: evaluation runway & legal sequencing for OptiMed pilot
messages:

Subject: Pilot MAP & timeline questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the product demo yesterday — the team found the latency and privacy options promising. Procurement asked me to capture a short MAP so we can align internal stakeholders (security, legal, ops) and unblock an executive decision by end of September.

High-level asks from our side:
- A one-page MAP with evaluation milestones and gating criteria (pilot -> production)
- Expected evidence for SOC2, retention controls, and data flow diagrams
- Proposed sequencing for MSA/DPA and order form so we can align our legal reviews

Would you share a suggested MAP and a timeline we can tuck into our SOW? We have a hard deployment window starting Nov 1.

Best,
Diana Clark
Director, Strategic Partnerships
OptiMed Health

Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & timeline questions

Diana — thanks for the clear ask and for hosting the demo. I attached a first-pass MAP that maps evaluation milestones to legal/procurement checkpoints and a short evidence packet.

Key points up front:
- MAP run (pilot): 4 weeks (functional + performance validation). Gate to production = acceptance checklist + SOC2 evidence review.
- Legal sequencing we recommend: 1) DPA + security exhibit concurrent with pilot, 2) MSA redlines during pilot so order form can be signed at acceptance, 3) Order form executed as last step to enable billing and reserved capacity. This minimizes legal blockers at go-live.
- Critical dependencies: SOC2 artifacts (we shared), KMS scope, and whether you require a private deployment (VPC/on-prem). Those affect the order form timeline.

I've cc'd Ben (sales ops) for procurement flow and Karthik (contracts) for milestone-aware redlines.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the attached MAP_OptiMed_v1.xlsx and confirm any internal milestone names.
2) If you want us to, we can run a 30-minute joint legal/procurement sync with your counsel next week.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — adding a quick procurement note.

From a procurement perspective, the sequence Marissa outlined is the least disruptive: we can attach provisional pricing to the MAP so finance can model cost with/without dedicated capacity. A couple of practical things to speed review:
- We can provide a clean order form template with variables pre-filled (seat counts, reserved GPU tiers, expected token volumes).
- If OptiMed needs an accelerated signature, we usually recommend the legal team sign a narrow, pilot-scoped order form that limits spend but enables a short-term commitment. Finalized MSA can follow.

If you share the internal approval gates, I can craft the order form draft and a procurement checklist this week.

—Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Diana Clark <diana.clark@optimed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & timeline questions

Diana / Marissa — I reviewed the MAP_OptiMed_v1 spreadsheet and sketched a milestone-aware sequencing for agreements. High level:

1) Pre-pilot (T-2 weeks):
   - Execute a minimal DPA + security addendum that references SOC2 artifacts and sets data residency controls. This is lightweight and clears operational questions.

2) Pilot period (weeks 0–4):
   - DPA in place; pilot-scoped order form (pilot scope/term/cost) signed to allow provisioning.
   - Technical acceptance tests run; Redwood provides temporary access for your security/infosec review.

3) Acceptance (week 4):
   - Run acceptance checklist (functional + latency + security gating). If pass, transition to final order form.

4) Post-acceptance (T+1 week):
   - MSA redlines closed and attached to final order form; SOC2 complete for go-live (or SOC2 in-scope evidence provided).

Risks / notes:
- If OptiMed requires bespoke KMS/HSM integration, that will push order form finalization by 2–3 weeks.
- We can add an explicit rollback/fallback in the MAP (automated throttling + alternate region) to address uptime SLAs during pilot.

I'll attach a draft MSA excerpt showing the acceptance and order form dependency language (redwood-msadpa-draft.docx). Happy to join your legal sync on Wed.

Karthik Iyer
Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-msadpa-draft.docx
From: Diana Clark <diana.clark@optimed.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & timeline questions

Team — this is very helpful, thanks. I reviewed the MAP and the sequencing looks workable for our board timeline. A few clarifying items from procurement and legal:

- Can you flag any acceptance test artifacts we should include as evidence (example: sample traces, token summaries, perf graphs)?
- Our security lead asked for a short KMS integration plan if we decide on private deployment. Can Redwood provide an estimated effort and impact to go-live?
- For the pilot order form, we'd prefer a 30-day capped spend approach (billing enabled but capped) — that should keep our CFO comfortable.

Let's do the legal sync on Wednesday at 10am PT; I invited our counsel (procurement@optimed.com) to the invite. If you can circulate the pilot order form template beforehand, procurement will review it during the call.

I'll confirm after the meeting whether we push forward with VPC or hosted.

Best,
Diana
Director, Strategic Partnerships
OptiMed Health
